LESSON: THE PERIODIC TABLE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Matter and Chemical Reactions
Topic 2.1: The Periodic Table
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Periodic Table, part of Matter and Chemical Reactions in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: Why is electron arrangement significant? 2. How are elements arranged in the periodic table?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Periodic Table together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: as the learner sorts and arranges the first twenty elements of the periodic table

according to their similarities.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner models the electron configuration of any five elements of the periodic table

using locally available materials.

Values:
● Respect: as the learner recognises and respects the input of every group member as they discuss how to determine the

valence and oxidation numbers of elements and radicals.

● Unity: as the learner takes turns in playing roles when drawing dot (.) and cross (x) diagrams to illustrate ion formation

for atoms of elements of the periodic table.

● Responsibility: as the learner uses digital devices with assistive technology appropriately to watch simulations and

animations on ion formation and keeps them safely after use.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

• Life skills, moral education and human sexuality education – Problem solving skills: as the learner arranges the first

twenty elements of the periodic table into groups and periods.

• Socio Economic and environmental issues - Financial literacy: as the learner uses locally available materials as a way

of minimising the expenses when modelling the electron configuration of any five elements of the periodic table.

Suggested Learning Resources:

● Digital devices with assistive technology such as screen readers and magnifiers,

● Print textbooks in appropriate font and colour,
